subject: Error in readModel when reading a latent class model

messages.author: d0451acd9a715392
messages.subject: Error in readModel when reading a latent class model
parts:
Hi All

I am trying to read the output of a latent class model with 8 classes (Mplus 7.2 output file attached), but I get this error:

Error in mat[r, ] <- line : 
  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length
In addition: Warning messages:
1: NAs introduced by coercion 
2: NAs introduced by coercion 

I read the response to Patrick Miller in this blog (28/08/2013) and downloaded the patch, but I get the same error.

Any suggestion would be greatly appreciated.

Many thanks

Annibale

messages.author: 644e1c01c3c42210
messages.subject: Re: Error in readModel when reading a latent class model
parts:
Hi Annibale,

Thanks for forwarding the problematic output file. It turns out that this file contains a new section header "Available post-processing tools:" that I had never seen before (probably new in v7.2?), which was throwing off the section parser. I have added this header to the list and your file now parses correctly. Incidentally, your residuals output also had section headers named "Model Estimated Means" instead of the typical "Model Estimated Means/Intercepts/Thresholds", so your residuals were also not being parsed. I added the new section naming to the residuals parser, too. Both of these problems underscore how fragile the text parsing approach can be for reading Mplus output files... If one section header changes or is added, there's no way to catch it until a problematic output file is identified. Anyhow, these problems are fixed in the development version on Github. I'm planning to roll out recent changes to CRAN soon, too.

Best,
Michael

Hi Michael

many thanks for you prompt reply. I was not hoping to have a solution so quickly!

I perfectly understand the problems of parsing a text file with heading which change depending on the model and the version and subversion of Mplus!
Mplus developers should provide some lower level access to Mplus output and input. It would make we R users very happy.

Thanks you for you great job.

Annibale
